estimatedSavingsNotes: Anonymous ingest still stores priority guest batches but no longer writes behavioral timeline facts in the request path.
Permanent invalid analytics bodies return non-retryable 4xx responses instead of creating retry storms.
Consent-denied analytics calls are acknowledged without a per-request diagnostic write.
Identified event fact ingestion now uses deterministic create conflicts for dedupe instead of reading first.
Non-priority event fact rollups queue into minute batches while priority purchase, unlock, viewer, and watch events keep immediate rollup coverage.
BigQuery event-triggered exports still cheap-exit on not-due windows and repeated failure status writes are TTL-suppressed.

fixesApplied.detail: Priority guest batch writes remain in the transaction, while session reads, per-request consent diagnostics, inline behavioral timeline writes, and retryable permanent failures were removed or capped.
Identified event facts use deterministic document create conflicts for dedupe, trigger dedupe uses create conflict instead of a read, and non-priority facts queue into minute rollup batches.
Existing daily/window export guards, watermark batches, query guardrails, readiness TTL, and cheap event-trigger exits were kept, with TTL suppression added for repeated failure status writes.

deferredFindings.reason: This pass touched the requested anonymous ingest route and Functions event-fact lane. The separate identified HTTP ingest route still needs its own freshness review before moving any known-user materialization work.
deferredFindings.nextStep: Run a focused pass on /api/analytics/ingest-identified with known-user index freshness tests.

deferredFindings.reason: Non-priority event facts now queue into minute batches, but the dedicated minute-batch materializer should be built in the next scheduled analytics lane rather than in the hot-path route.
deferredFindings.nextStep: Add a scheduled non-priority rollup materializer that drains analytics_event_rollup_batches under the 24h cadence policy.

deferredFindings.reason: The source guard makes the current event trigger cheap for not-due windows. Fully removing the deployed trigger requires an explicit Functions deployment/config pass.
deferredFindings.nextStep: Promote scheduledBigQueryRawEventsExport through the Functions index and retire the event trigger in a deploy-scoped change.
